hits.label: beta arch
hits.definition: A supersecondary motif comprising two successive beta strands joined by a connecting segment, without hydrogen-bond pairing between the two flanking strands.

hits.label: membrane-facing lateral channel fenestration
hits.definition: A lateral passage through the transmembrane wall of a protein channel connecting its central pore cavity to the lipid-facing exterior, distinct from the main transmembrane pore axis.

synonyms.source: Curator scope distinction; lateral openings also occur in other contexts

hits.label: protein tunnel bottleneck
hits.definition: A region of a protein tunnel where the available radius along a specified pathway reaches its minimum in a stated coordinate and geometric model.

synonyms.source: Curator scope distinction; a local constriction need not be the path minimum

hits.label: membrane grommet activity
hits.definition: An activity in which a protein, or group of proteins, acts to restrict the size of a fenestration in a membrane or membrane system (i.e. restrict the diameter of a hole in a membrane). An example of this is the molecular function is performed by ESCRT-III proteins at the nuclear envelope of fission yeast during anaphase B.

hits.label: glomerular endothelium fenestra
hits.definition: A large plasma membrane-lined circular pore that perforates the flattened glomerular endothelium and, unlike those of other fenestrated capillaries, is not spanned by diaphragms; the density and size of glomerular fenestrae account, at least in part, for the high permeability of the glomerular capillary wall to water and small solutes.

hits.label: trabecular meshwork development
hits.definition: The progression of the trabecular meshwork over time, from its formation to the mature structure. The trabecular meshwork is a fenestrated endothelial-like tissue situated at the intersection of the cornea and the iris. The trabecular meshwork provides drainage for the aqueous humor.
